commit.message:
Point citation metadata at the concept DOI only

The v1.0.0 release was cut before the DOI existed, so the archived snapshot
did not contain its own DOI. Rather than pin a version DOI that goes stale on
every release, README and CITATION.cff now cite the concept DOI
(10.5281/zenodo.21855537), which always resolves to the latest version, and
point at the Zenodo record's Versions list for anyone who needs to pin one.

Tagging v1.0.1 from this commit so the archived snapshot and main match.

-`10.5281/zenodo.21855537` is the concept DOI and always resolves to the latest version. To cite this exact release, use `10.5281/zenodo.21855538`.
+`10.5281/zenodo.21855537` is the concept DOI: it always resolves to the latest version, which is what you normally want to cite. Every release also has its own version DOI, listed under **Versions** on the [Zenodo record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21855537), if you need to pin one exactly.
 
 GitHub renders a “Cite this repository” button from `CITATION.cff`.
